title: Optimal Condition for Initialization Variance in Deep Neural Networks: An SGD Dynamics Perspective
abstract: arXiv:2508.12834v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD), one of the most fundamental optimization algorithms in machine learning (ML), can be recast through a continuous-time approximation as a Fokker-Planck equation for Langevin dynamics, a viewpoint that has motivated many theoretical studies. Within this framework, we study the relationship between the quasi-stationary distribution derived from this equation and the initial distribution through the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. As the quasi-steady-state distribution depends on the expected cost function, the KL divergence eventually reveals the connection between the expected cost function and the initialization distribution. By applying this to deep neural network models (DNNs), we can express the bounds of the expected loss function explicitly in terms of the initialization parameters. translated_title: 深度神经网络初始化方差的最优条件：基于SGD动力学的视角
translated_abstract: 随机梯度下降（SGD）是机器学习中最基础的优化算法之一，通过连续时间近似可以将其重新表述为描述朗之万动力学的Fokker-Planck方程，这一视角已启发了众多理论研究。在该框架下，我们通过Kullback-Leibler（KL）散度研究了由该方程导出的准平稳分布与初始分布之间的关系。由于准稳态分布依赖于期望代价函数，KL散度最终揭示了期望代价函数与初始化分布之间的联系。将该方法应用于深度神经网络（DNN）模型后，我们可以用初始化参数显式地表达期望损失函数的界限。进而，通过最小化该界限，我们得到了高斯（初始化方差）的最优条件……
tldr: 该论文通过将SGD近似为朗之万动力学并利用Fokker-Planck方程与KL散度，建立了期望损失与初始化分布的联系，从而推导出深度神经网络初始化方差的最优条件。
en_tdlr: By recasting SGD as Langevin dynamics via the Fokker-Planck equation and relating the quasi-stationary distribution to the initialization distribution through KL divergence, this paper derives an optimal condition for initialization variance in deep neural networks by minimizing a bound on the expected loss.
